name: Moped
description: A limited-speed motor-driven cycle with wheels under 20 inches that can't exceed 30 mph on level ground; an electric one without pedals must have a motor under 2 gross brake horsepower (1,500 W) and meet the federal safety standards for motor-driven cycles. Defined by Idaho Code §49-114(9).

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels, each less than 20 inches in diameter
Its motor can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground

An electric one with no pedals has an automatic transmission, a motor under 2 gross brake horsepower (1,500 W), and as manufactured meets federal motor vehicle safety standards for motor-driven cycles
One with pedals falls under the general moped clause instead, which caps its speed at 30 mph but sets no motor power limit
Not an electric-assisted bicycle; a bike over the e-bike limits is a moped only if it fits this definition
One that can go faster than 30 mph is not a moped, and is a motor-driven cycle or motorcycle if it meets federal safety standards
Not titled, and ITD does not register it or issue it a license plate
No motorcycle endorsement needed to ride one
Not among the vehicles Idaho's under-18 helmet law covers
